stories.title: Humanitarian crisis worsening in refuge for civilians fleeing Sudan’s civil war
stories.summary: Conditions are deteriorating in city of El Obeid and camps on its outskirts, with more people arriving every day Humanitarian conditions in the Sudanese city of El Obeid and two camps on its outskirts are dire and deteriorating, according to people on the ground, as civilians displaced by fighting between the Sudanese Armed Forces and Rapid Support Forces (RSF) militia continue to pour in from the surrounding countryside. The UN says more than 15,000 families have arrived since mid-July, joining more than 200,000 people who arrived in the first half of the year, according to government figures cited by Save the Children. opening: Conditions are deteriorating in city of El Obeid and camps on its outskirts, with more people arriving every day Humanitarian conditions in the Sudanese city of El Obeid and two camps on its outskirts are dire and deteriorating, according to people on the ground, as civilians displaced by fighting between the Sudanese Armed Forces and Rapid Support Forces (RSF) militia continue to pour in from the surrounding countryside.

The UN says more than 15,000 families have arrived since mid-July, joining more than 200,000 people who arrived in the first half of the year, according to government figures cited by Save the Children.

stories.title: Charity thanks inmates for work to save hedgehogs
stories.summary: An animal charity has thanked prison inmates for helping to save hedgehogs' lives. Prisoners in HMP La Moye, in St Brelade, have given Jersey Hedgehog Preservation Group 20 feeding and nesting boxes which they have made out of reclaimed pallet timber. Peter Gould, the prison's vocational manager, said the work could help reduce reoffending because it taught inmates skills to support future employment and helped them feel they were contributing to the community. Dru Burdon, from the hedgehog group, said: "If it helps with carpentry skills training, so much the better, these boxes are certainly saving hedgehogs' lives." Gould said the project also taught health and safety best practice and gave prisoners experience of using machinery and equipment. "For some, the project provides a valuable introduction to skills that could lead to recognised qualifications and careers in the construction industry." He said the project helped inmates have a "sense of purpose, achievement and connection to the community" which was "incredibly valuable". Burdon said the scheme had developed from a chance meeting with a prison officer at the vets. She said: "He found a little hedgehog in need of care and we got talking, so the upshot was that I gave them the templates for both nesting and feeding boxes." She said of the 20 boxes the prisoners had given the charity earlier in August, all the feeding boxes had sold out and raised £20 each and there were just a few £25 nesting boxes left. "The response from the public and our members has been terrific," she added. Gould said the hedgehog boxes formed part of a wider programme of vocational projects at the prison.
